text:
maya: Customer reports SSO failing after IdP rotated certs. Error in our logs: "SAML signature verification failed: no matching signing key". They can still fetch metadata URL but login returns 403.

samir: Can you paste the metadata URL and a copy of the exact error payload from our side? Also any way to repro locally?

maya: Metadata: https://idp.example-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml
I ran a quick fetch: `curl -sS https://idp.example-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml | head -n 60` and saw the KeyDescriptor block looks weird.

maya: ```xml
<md:EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.example-corp.com/">
  <md:IDPSSODescriptor protocolSupportEnumeration="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:protocol">
    <md:KeyDescriptor use="encryption">
      <ds:KeyInfo>
        <ds:X509Data>
          <ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...NEW_CERT...==</ds:X509Certificate>
        </ds:X509Data>
      </ds:KeyInfo>
    </md:KeyDescriptor>
    <!-- no KeyDescriptor with use="signing" present -->
  </md:IDPSSODescriptor>
</md:EntityDescriptor>
```

kelly: Ahh, they rotated keys but marked the new key use="encryption" instead of use="signing" (common mistake when key rotation is automated by the IdP). Our verifier picks KeyDescriptor[@use="signing"] for signature validation and ignores encryption keys by default.

samir: Can you confirm our metadata fetcher actually sees that element? Sometimes proxies add whitespace or we fetch a cached copy. Run: `curl -sI https://idp.example-corp.com/saml/metadata.xml`

maya: Output: 
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/xml; charset=utf-8
Cache-Control: max-age=300
Last-Modified: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:22:01 GMT
```
(no redirects, TTL=300s)

supportbot: SAML metadata for tenant "example-corp" last fetched 2026-02-10T12:22:31Z, cached for 300s. If invalid, use tenant console to upload metadata or call the manual refresh API.

kelly: Two immediate remediation paths: 1) Ask IdP admin to change KeyDescriptor use to "signing" for the cert used to sign assertions OR add a distinct signing key entry. 2) Temporary workaround: customer can upload the X.509 certificate directly into our SSO config (Tenant Settings → SAML → Upload IdP certificate) so we have the exact public key to verify signatures while they fix metadata.

samir: Also note we could relax verifier heuristics to accept KeyDescriptor use="encryption" when no signing key exists, but that is a change with security implications — need eng-ml approval. For immediate support: tell customer to upload certificate.

maya: Customer asked for exact steps. samir / kelly can you paste the console steps and the manual refresh API we can run after they update metadata?

samir: Steps: 1) Console > Admin > Security > SAML settings for tenant. 2) Paste the cert (PEM block without headers) into "IdP signing certificate" and save. 3) To force our metadata fetch (if they fix metadata instead of uploading), POST to our internal endpoint: `POST https://console.redwood.ai/internal/saml/tenants/example-corp/refresh` with service token (ops only). Note: this bypasses the 300s cache and will reparse the updated metadata immediately.

kelly: Also tell them to check the metadata for multiple KeyDescriptor entries — some IdPs emit the same cert twice with different use attributes; the correct practice is to include an explicit signing key. Example fix snippet to give the IdP team: 
```xml
<md:KeyDescriptor use="signing">
  <ds:KeyInfo>...their cert...</ds:KeyInfo>
</md:KeyDescriptor>
```

maya: Sent instructions to customer (they are willing to upload cert). I'll get the PEM and upload. After upload I'll ping here and we can run the refresh if they also update metadata. :thumbsup:

supportbot: Action logged: ticket #TCK-12345 updated, awaiting customer cert upload.

maya: Uploaded the cert, ran sign-in test — still failing. Our logs now show: "SAML signature verification failed: key mismatch". I suspect I pasted without the headers earlier. Trying again.

maya: Re-uploaded with full PEM headers `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`/`-----END CERTIFICATE-----`. Retested; login succeeded. Customer confirms SSO working. :tada:

kelly: Great. Follow-up: I'll create a short KB note for this pattern (rotated certs with wrong use attribute) and propose a small parser tweak to try encryption keys as a fallback if no signing key present, but only after security review.

samir: Filing eng ticket for evaluation.

maya: Closing loop with customer. Thanks team.
